title: Runtime inference forensics interactive walkthrough - Arcadia Retail
summary: Interactive console walkthrough focused on tracing, request-level forensics, and error analysis. Demonstrated request playback, KV cache fallthrough detection, model fallback routing, and SLO/latency breakdowns. Discussed security/compliance needs (SOC 2, SSO, KMS), POC scope, and benchmark run next week.
topics: model variant fallbacks and routing policies
next steps: POC benchmark and security package
next_steps: Alex to send SOC 2 + security whitepaper and KMS integration notes
Schedule 2-hour POC benchmark session for week of 2027-07-26
Maya to prep sample workload script and latency/cost dashboard template
Customer to provide 500 representative requests and target SLOs
action_items: Alex Kim - share SOC2 pack, KMS notes, and pricing sheet - due 2027-07-26
Maya Patel - create POC benchmark script and dashboard template - due 2027-07-25
Samir Gupta (Arcadia) - upload 500 sample requests to shared bucket and confirm p95 SLO - due 2027-07-24
Lena Ortiz (Arcadia) - confirm encryption at rest requirements & KMS/HSM vendor - due 2027-07-28
transcript:
Header: Date: 2027-07-22 15:00 PDT | Duration: 53m | Redwood: Alex Kim (AE), Maya Patel (SE), Diego Ramos (Product) | Arcadia: Jordan Lee (Head of Platform), Priya Banerjee (SRE), Samir Gupta (ML Eng), Lena Ortiz (Security)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, really glad to be here. quick intro — I'm Alex, AE for the west region, with Maya our solutions eng and Diego from product.
[00:10] Jordan (Arcadia): Thanks, Alex. Jordan here. We're excited to see the console playbook you're talking about — particularly how we can map requests to traces and figure out why some inference calls go sideways.
[00:20] Maya (Redwood): Awesome. Today's plan: we'll show live request playback, how request IDs map to model runs, KV cache hits vs miss detection, and the fallback routing when dedicated capacity is saturated. We'll also show latency/cost per route. Questions before we dive in?
[00:30] Priya (Arcadia): Just to set context — our production inference runs on a mix of hosted endpoints and an on-prem private cluster for regulated SKUs. P95 latency target is 150ms for interactive queries, and anything above 250ms is a problem. We also have strict retention rules — 30 days for request logs.
[00:45] Alex (Redwood): Good to know. We'll show the timeline and filter by retention windows and you can see redactions.
[00:55] [01:00] Maya (Redwood): I'm sharing my screen — opening the Runtime Forensics tab in the console. One note: transcription may spell product names funny — our internal name is Redwood Optimize — sometimes the auto transcript writes it as Red wood Opti. ignore that.
[01:20] [01:30] Maya (Redwood): Ok first, here is a request list. You can search by request_id, user_id, or route. I'm going to pick a request that failed with a model fallback. You can see at 0.00 the initial enqueue, then 45ms later the model 13b was selected, but then we had a KV cache miss and a fallback to a quantized variant.
[01:50] Samir (Arcadia): When you say KV cache miss can you show the indicators? We had an incident where the cache thrashing created huge tail latencies last month.
[02:05] Maya (Redwood): Yep — in the timeline you'll see a green block for 'KV cache hit', yellow for 'prefetch', red for 'KV cache miss' — also a small note that sometimes the transcript or the event name shows as "KV cash" which annoyed me in the logs — transcription issues. But here's the miss, see the spike in token compute after the miss.
[02:30] [03:00] Jordan (Arcadia): Is the miss detection deterministic? Could we get false positives when we do partial key sets?
[03:10] Maya (Redwood): Good question. Detection combines the request prefix fingerprint and the runtime cache lookup. We mark a miss when the runtime had to fetch embeddings/keys from main memory and there's a corresponding delta in compute time. There are heuristics so very short prefixes can look like misses — we annotate those as 'probable miss'. We surface confidence scores.
[03:35] Priya (Arcadia): Are those confidence scores available via API? We need programmatic alerts.
[03:40] Maya (Redwood): Yes — both the console and the API expose the raw events. You can subscribe to cache_miss events and push to your alerting.
[03:50] [04:00] Alex (Redwood): Another critical piece is model fallback routing — when you have dedicated pools full, the smart router will route to a cheaper quantized variant or to hosted lane with a different latency. We'll show an example of an automatic fallback that kept the app alive but at a different latency and quality tier.
[04:20] [04:30] Maya (Redwood): Here's a request where the policy says prefer dedicated, else fallback to hosted low-cost. Notice the quality flag in the trace — we log the model id, quantization, and a quality estimate (we call it Q-score in the console). Note: sometimes the console transcribes Q-score as 'cue score' if audio is bad — ignore that.
[04:55] Samir (Arcadia): How do you capture quality regressions? We need regression detection tied to a set of prompts.
[05:05] Maya (Redwood): We integrate Optimize-style evals — you can pin a prompt set and the console will run diffs when we swap model variants. It generates an alert on semantic drift beyond thresholds. We can wire that to your slack.
[05:20] [06:00] Jordan (Arcadia): Walk me through a real failure scenario — like the one we saw earlier this quarter where certain routes had intermittent 400s and some 502s.
[06:15] Maya (Redwood): Sure — pulling an example. This one shows a 502 returned from the runtime because KV cache backend timed out. In the trace you can see: initial request, cache lookup, timeout event, then fallback model selection, then final return to caller with 200 but with degraded tokens per second. We also keep the raw stderr captured for the runtime error — redacted per retention policy.
[06:40] Priya (Arcadia): Can we see the actual error text? For compliance we sometimes need stack snippets for RCA. 
[06:50] Diego (Redwood): We can surface error snippets but by default they are redacted in the hosted logs. For Dedicated and Private you can enable verbose logs stored in your VPC and integrate with your SIEM. We'll include retention and redaction options in the security pack.
[07:10] [07:30] Lena (Arcadia): On the SOC2 note — do you have audit logs for who accessed request payloads? We need user-level access trails and SSO.
[07:40] Alex (Redwood): Yes — audit trail per token and per-user. We support SAML SSO and RBAC, and KMS for encryption keys. We also integrate with HSM providers if required. We'll send the SOC 2 evidence and the HSM integration notes after the call.
[08:00] Samir (Arcadia): Back to traces — how granular are timestamps? We need sub-10ms resolution for distributed tracing.
[08:10] Maya (Redwood): Our runtime timestamps are microsecond-resolution in the trace, but the console UI shows ms. You can export raw traces in newline-delimited JSON for post-hoc analysis.
[08:25] [09:00] Jordan (Arcadia): One pain point for us is mapping external request IDs (from our frontend) to the runtime request_id. How do you correlate?
[09:15] Maya (Redwood): We have a header mapping — you can pass x-arcadia-request-id and the console will show both ids. You can also configure a mapping rule so the external id is primary in the UI.
[09:30] Priya (Arcadia): Can we add custom tags to filter traces by customer_id or experiment flags?
[09:40] Maya (Redwood): Yep — metadata tags come through the request payload and are indexed. There are size limits and sanitized fields — we'll share the limits.
[09:50] [10:00] Alex (Redwood): Now I want to show the request playback — Maya will re-run the request against a pinned model in a sandbox. This helps reproduce flakies. Maya?
[10:10] Maya (Redwood): Running playback now. You'll see the timeline advance and a side-by-side diff of tokens. Playback supports three modes: exact replay (same input), sandbox with synthetic token seeding, and A/B with two model variants.
[10:30] [11:00] Maya (Redwood): Ok playback finished. Note the difference: the original had a small dropout at token 42 because the runtime retried a failed KV fetch. Playback shows the retry pattern and we annotate the retry type (fast/linear backoff).
[11:20] Samir (Arcadia): Is playback deterministic? If we replay after a model update will tokens differ?
[11:30] Maya (Redwood): If the model weights changed you'll get different tokens. Playback includes a 'model signature' header that pins model version and quantization. For critical repros we recommend pinning an exact model hash in the POC.
[11:50] [12:30] Jordan (Arcadia): What about SLO dashboards — can we slice by customer, route, and model variant?
[12:40] Maya (Redwood): Yes — the console has templated SLO dashboards. You can build custom widgets to show p50/p95/p99 latency, cost per token, and error rate by model. You can also set auto-alerts if p95 crosses threshold.
[13:00] [13:30] Priya (Arcadia): We had an event where batch sizes increased and that spiked latency. Can your console show batch size distribution correlated with latency?
[13:45] Maya (Redwood): Absolutely — sampler events include batch size and GPU utilization. We show a heatmap of batch distribution over time. If you want, we can also correlate with autoscale events.
[14:10] [15:00] Alex (Redwood): Quick tangent — cost controls: token breakdown by prefix vs generation and suggestions for quantization. Diego, may want to add any product notes here.
[15:20] Diego (Redwood): Yeah, we run an Optimize analysis that looks at sequence length distributions and suggests quantization profiles or batching windows. For Arcadia with short interactive queries, we often suggest enabling prefix caching and a medium quant profile to hit latency SLOs while reducing unit cost.
[15:50] Samir (Arcadia): Is the Optimize analysis automated or a manual report? We have 20 routes so manual is too heavy.
[16:05] Diego (Redwood): It's automated — you can run it on historical traces, and it produces recommendations ranked by estimated cost savings and expected latency impact. You can accept them through the console as a change set.
[16:25] [17:00] Jordan (Arcadia): Security again — if we run a private deployment on-prem will we still get the same tracing fidelity?
[17:10] Maya (Redwood): Yes — the private control plane ships with the same agent and the traces are collected locally then optionally mirrored to Redwood's console if you opt in. For air-gapped installs we provide an on-prem analytics bundle.
[17:30] Lena (Arcadia): Do you support field encryption or token-level redaction? We cannot log PII in plaintext.
[17:40] Alex (Redwood): Field-level redaction is supported. You can configure redaction rules and a scrubber pipeline. We also support envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS.
[17:55] [18:30] Priya (Arcadia): Ok, let's talk about the POC: we want to run a week-long benchmark against 500 sample requests, measure median and p95 for dedicated vs hosted fallback, and validate cost numbers. Can we do that?
[18:45] Maya (Redwood): Absolutely. We'll run the benchmark from a dedicated pool sized to your expected concurrency, and then simulate the overload to exercise fallback rules. We'll export the traces and send a benchmark report.
[19:05] Samir (Arcadia): For the overload simulation, can you mimic network jitter and KV backend slowness? That's what caused our last incident.
[19:15] Maya (Redwood): We can add fault injection to the POC harness — introduce artificial latency on the KV layer and on the network. That will surface fallback and retry behavior.
[19:30] [20:00] Jordan (Arcadia): How do you recommend we instrument our app headers to make troubleshooting faster?
[20:10] Maya (Redwood): Send both x-arcadia-request-id and a user_session_id; include route and experiment tags. Also include a short stack trace capture for client errors. We'll share a small middleware snippet — Samir, you'll like it — that auto-injects these headers.
[20:30] Samir (Arcadia): Great.
[20:40] [21:00] Alex (Redwood): Quick note on compliance: we'll redact the actual prompt text in the hosted logs by default, but for the POC we can enable dev-mode which keeps raw prompts in a secure bucket for debugging. This has to be agreed in the security addendum.
[21:20] Lena (Arcadia): We'll want the dev-mode turned off after debugging window. We need an attestation.
[21:30] Alex (Redwood): Sure — we'll include an attestation template.
[21:40] [22:00] Maya (Redwood): I'm going to show a more complex trace where a batch coalescing event increased per-request latency. See here at the 2:13 mark of the trace — batch size went from 1–3 to 16 and GPU deschedule occurred. You can click into the GPU metric and see the utilization spike.
[22:25] Priya (Arcadia): Can that be prevented by different autoscale policies?
[22:35] Maya (Redwood): Yes — we show autoscale event triggers and have recommended policies. For interactive SLOs we recommend aggressive min-instances to avoid big batch coalescing. The console can simulate expected tail latency for candidate autoscale configs.
[22:55] [24:00] Jordan (Arcadia): About model versioning — can we pin specific versions and do gradual rollouts?
[24:10] Maya (Redwood): Yes — rollout policies support canary percentages, A/B, and automatic rollout pauses if quality or latency regressions are detected. All of that is visible in the rollout history.
[24:40] Samir (Arcadia): If a canary fails we want immediate rollback and a human in the loop for RCA. How fast are automated rollbacks?
[24:55] Diego (Redwood): Rollbacks are immediate upon policy breach — they happen within the same routing decision layer. You can configure safety windows and require manual approval for production.
[25:20] [26:00] Maya (Redwood): Another neat feature is the error-correlation graph — it clusters similar error stacks across requests and surfaces probable root causes. It's a mix of heuristics and a bit of ML.
[26:20] Priya (Arcadia): Does the clustering ever surface false clusters? We had that with a previous vendor where unrelated user errors were grouped.
[26:30] Maya (Redwood): We expose the clustering confidence and you can tune thresholds. In our experience you get good signal for runtime errors, but client errors sometimes need domain-specific rules.
[26:50] [28:00] Jordan (Arcadia): Talking timelines — if we sign up for a POC, how long to stand up dedicated pool and run the benchmark?
[28:10] Alex (Redwood): For a standard POC we can provision a dedicated pool within 48 hours given a signed order and initial data. Private deployments are longer — depends on network onboarding.
[28:30] Samir (Arcadia): Cost — how will you bill the POC?
[28:40] Alex (Redwood): POCs are usually credit-based — we'll provide an estimated token and GPU-hour budget. If you go to production we'll roll that into the enterprise contract.
[28:55] [30:00] Maya (Redwood): I'm going to export the trace and kick off a quick benchmark job against your 50-sample subset to show expected outputs — this is a smoke run.
[30:10] Samir (Arcadia): Cool.
[30:20] [31:00] Maya (Redwood): Smoke run completed, uploading the results to the shared folder. Quick note: in the console you can annotate traces — I'll add comments on three suspicious traces. You can also pin them to the incident.
[31:25] Jordan (Arcadia): Nice. Can you also add a link to the middleware snippet in the notes?
[31:35] Maya (Redwood): Done. It's in the meeting notes.
[31:45] [33:00] Lena (Arcadia): A quick question on data residency — some of our EU traffic needs to stay in EU regions. Can region routing be enforced at request routing layer?
[33:10] Alex (Redwood): Yes — routing policies include region constraints and we can pin traffic to EU-only endpoints.
[33:30] Priya (Arcadia): Are there costs for region-restricted routing?
[33:35] Diego (Redwood): Minimal network egress differences may apply; we'll include that in the pricing sheet.
[33:50] [35:00] Samir (Arcadia): About observability retention — what's the max retention for traces in hosted?
[35:10] Alex (Redwood): By default 30 days for traces and 90 days for aggregated metrics; extended retention is an add-on. For Dedicated we can match your retention requirements on contract.
[35:40] [36:00] Maya (Redwood): I'm adding a final reproduction: a KV timeout injected and we see how the request path forks to fallback and also increases cost per token. You'll see cost estimate on the right.
[36:20] Jordan (Arcadia): For our cost modeling we need a per-route cost delta when you fall back to hosted vs dedicated. Can you provide that in the POC report?
[36:30] Maya (Redwood): Yes — we'll include a per-route delta and quantized variant impact.
[36:50] [38:00] Alex (Redwood): Ok we're nearing the end — recap time. Jordan, are the success criteria still: p95 < 150ms for interactive routes, verified fallback behavior under load, and verified no PII leakage in logs?
[38:15] Jordan (Arcadia): Yes. Also provide a template attestation that dev-mode was time-limited.
[38:25] Alex (Redwood): Perfect. Final questions?
[38:30] Priya (Arcadia): One small thing — when you show the SDK snippet can you include go and java examples?
[38:40] Maya (Redwood): Yes — we'll include go, java, python and node snippets.
[38:50] Samir (Arcadia): Any mention of other vendors? We talked earlier about GoliathAI and CloudEndpointX in our evaluation.
[39:00] Alex (Redwood): We discussed differences — mainly around tracing fidelity and deployment flexibility. We'll include a short competitor note.
[39:15] [40:00] Maya (Redwood): Ok I'm uploading the security pack and the SOC 2 summary to the shared folder now. Alex will follow up with pricing and the POC contract.
[40:30] Jordan (Arcadia): Good. Thanks everyone.
[40:40] Alex (Redwood): Thanks — next steps: Alex to send docs, Maya to create benchmark harness, Arcadia to provide requests. We'll capture these as action items in the follow-up email.
[40:55] [41:30] (crosstalk) Samir (Arcadia): One last curious thing — do you have a feature to map user complaints in support tickets to traces automatically?
[41:40] Maya (Redwood): There's an integration with our incident correlator — you can paste ticket ids and it will try to find matching traces using heuristics and the external request id header. Not perfect but helpful.
[41:55] [43:00] Jordan (Arcadia): Alright closing — we'll aim to get the sample requests uploaded by Friday. Thanks all.
[43:10] Alex (Redwood): Thanks, talk soon.
[43:20] [end]
